# Launcher Offline

> Free, open-source Windows app (MIT) that puts PC game launchers into their official offline mode with one click, by adding a Windows Firewall rule that blocks only the launcher's internet access. It solves two common problems: launchers logging you out when two PCs share one account, and launchers repeatedly asking for a password or 2FA code before a single-player game can start.

- Supported launchers: Ubisoft Connect (tested with Far Cry 6), Epic Games Launcher (tested; press "Continue in Offline Mode"), Rockstar Games Launcher, EA app, Battle.net (not tested yet). Steam is not supported: it allows several PCs per account, and when blocked the current client does not enter offline mode.
- Install: run `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cngil/launcher-offline/main/install.ps1 | iex` in PowerShell, or download the ZIP and double-click `LauncherOffline.cmd`. Windows 10/11, no build step, Windows PowerShell 5.1.
- Use: sign in to the launcher and start the game once while online, then press "Go offline" in the app. "Go online" undoes it; "Remove all blocks" removes every rule.
- It does not modify games, launcher settings, DRM, the hosts file or registry settings. It only works with games the user owns and has activated.
- Firewall rules are grouped as "LauncherOffline". Launchers installed through Scoop junctions are supported; "Repair" re-points rules after launcher updates.
- Languages: English, Turkish; new languages are one file in `locales/`. New launchers are one data file in `launchers/`.
